::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
**I am on the job market** for postdoctoral and research scientist positions starting in 2027.
If my work fits your group, please [get in touch](mailto:polejua@email.sc.edu).
:::

I am a Ph.D. candidate in Biostatistics at the Arnold School of Public Health, University of
South Carolina, advised by Dr. Alexander McLain. I expect to graduate in May 2027. I live in
the Dallas–Fort Worth area of Texas.

My work is in **functional data analysis** and **scalable Bayesian methods**. Many health
studies now measure each person many times, over a day or over years, so each person gives a
curve or a distribution instead of a single number. I develop methods that use the whole curve,
test them with simulation studies, apply them to real data, and write them as software that
other people can use.

I am open to many different applications of these methods: from wearable data to genomics,
nutrition, agriculture, air pollution, and many other applications. So far, I have applied them
to wearable accelerometer data and genomic data.

## What I work on

::: {.card-row}
::: {.item}
#### Variational Bayes for high-dimensional regression
Fast Bayesian variable selection with spike-and-slab priors that keeps the uncertainty
honest. R package `spexvb` on CRAN.
:::
::: {.item}
#### Scalar-on-function regression
Bayesian regression where the predictor is a curve, for example 24-hour activity from a
wrist accelerometer.
:::
::: {.item}
#### Wearable and accelerometer data
Clustering 24-hour activity patterns, processing raw accelerometer data with GGIR, and
measuring the bias of non-wear imputation.
:::
:::

## Where I am going

I want to see statistical methods used in the world, not only published. My goal is to work
with functional and intensive longitudinal data, from wearable devices or other sources,
developing methods and applying my own methods and those of others, so that practitioners can
use them. That can happen in academia or in industry, for example in a company that builds
wearable devices. More in [my own words](story.qmd).
